matched.set_a_axis: From lonely self-protection to relationally grounded stewardship
matched.set_b_axis: From lonely self-assertion to relational belonging
matched.overlap_description: Both describe Laurie moving from isolation, guardedness, and self-containment toward a socially integrated identity rooted in care, belonging, and interdependence.

matched.set_a_axis: From aimless indulgence to disciplined usefulness
matched.set_b_axis: From idle impulsiveness to steady self-command
matched.overlap_description: Both track Laurie’s movement away from idleness, drift, and playful self-indulgence toward discipline, purpose, and responsible action.

matched.set_a_axis: From singular romantic fixation to mature reciprocal love
matched.set_b_axis: From romantic fantasy to emotionally truthful love
matched.overlap_description: Both capture the shift from Jo-centered idealization and romantic fantasy to a more mature, reciprocal, reality-based love with Amy.

matched.set_a_axis: From defensive pride to chastened self-knowledge
matched.set_b_axis: From playful charm to ethical responsibility
matched.overlap_description: These are not identical, but they overlap in the later-stage moral maturation of Laurie: he becomes more self-aware, receptive to correction, and ethically serious.

unique_to_a.axis: From defensive pride to chastened self-knowledge

unique_to_b.axis: From playful charm to ethical responsibility

matched.set_a_axis: From playful intimacy to relinquished love
matched.set_b_axis: From playful fascination to transformed lifelong affection
matched.overlap_description: Both describe the Jo relationship as moving from intimate youthful closeness through romantic loss to a stable, non-possessive post-romantic bond.

matched.set_a_axis: From family friend to chosen partner
matched.set_b_axis: From teasing acquaintance to chosen life partner
matched.overlap_description: Both describe Amy’s relationship with Laurie as evolving from warm familiarity and admiration into marriage and adult partnership.

matched.set_a_axis: From wary obedience to mutual dependence
matched.set_b_axis: From sheltered grandson to dutiful companion
matched.overlap_description: Both track the grandfather-grandson bond from constraint and dependence toward mutual respect, duty, and aligned responsibility.

unique_to_a.axis: From neighboring outsider to quasi-family member

unique_to_b.axis: From sheltered grandson to dutiful companion

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From lonely self-assertion to relational belonging
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Starts as a shy, isolated boy whose selfhood is marked by confinement, boredom, and guarded separateness; his agency is expressed more as self-containment than confident mastery.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a socially integrated, emotionally settled man whose identity is grounded in family belonging, interdependence, and generous participation in others' lives, while retaining adult self-command.

trajectory.position_description: He begins lonely, bashful, and watchful, drawn toward the Marches but still separated from them. His desire for contact is present, but it is filtered through distance and self-protection.
key_moments: Curious interest in the March family and Jo
Loneliness and boredom in his sickroom

trajectory.position_description: He moves toward communion by seeking the March household, helping in crises, and becoming emotionally nourished by their company. His agency increasingly takes the form of stewardship rather than separation.
key_moments: Becomes a regular, trusted presence in the March home
Helps during Mrs. March's absence and Beth's illness

trajectory.position_description: His communion is tested by pride, rejection, and grief. He briefly reasserts himself through wounded withdrawal, but criticism and crisis redirect him toward maturity and responsibility.
key_moments: Prank and quarrel with Mr. Laurence
Return to duty and practical usefulness

trajectory.position_description: He settles into adult communion through marriage, family life, and philanthropic usefulness. His identity is no longer organized around proving himself or escaping constraint, but around sustaining others.
key_moments: Support of Jo's school and family circle

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s arc moves decisively from isolation and guarded selfhood toward relational belonging. Both analyses agree that his growth is not a loss of agency but its reorientation into care, family, and shared life.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From idle impulsiveness to steady self-command
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins as restless, charming, and prone to drift, with comfort and amusement often substituting for purpose.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a serious, industrious, and self-regulating adult who values work, restraint, and the responsible use of time and wealth.

trajectory.position_description: He enjoys companionship, music, games, and social ease, but his energy is undirected. He recognizes his own idleness only intermittently.
key_moments: Awareness of the March girls' industry

trajectory.position_description: Crisis and criticism force him to see his laziness and temper more clearly. He learns that his value lies in practical service, not just charm or leisure.
key_moments: Beth's illness and his practical helpfulness
Amy's frank lecture about his drifting

trajectory.position_description: He becomes more disciplined, seeking real work and living with greater restraint. His self-command is not perfect, but it is stable and sincere.
key_moments: Jo's letters describe him as improved
He admits he is not a genius composer
He turns toward business and practical usefulness
He acts as a steady husband and benefactor

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie clearly changes from a charmingly idle youth into a more disciplined adult. The combined evidence emphasizes both crisis-driven correction and later, durable self-command.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From romantic fantasy to emotionally truthful love
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins with idealized longing, especially toward Jo, and a tendency to dramatize feeling before fully understanding his own desire.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends with a realistic understanding of love as reciprocal, transformed, and compatible with duty; he accepts Amy as his true partner and treats his love for Jo as a completed youthful phase.

trajectory.position_description: He is deeply drawn to Jo and the March family, but his feelings remain playful, half-articulated, and romanticized. He does not yet fully understand the shape of his own desire.
key_moments: Growing emotional dependence on the March household

trajectory.position_description: Jo's refusal breaks the fantasy and forces him into grief, pride, and self-questioning. The old romantic story can no longer hold.
key_moments: Amy's criticism begins to reorient him

trajectory.position_description: He recognizes that his love for Jo has become non-romantic and that Amy is the woman who truly matches him. Love becomes mutual, adult, and grounded in shared values.
key_moments: He acknowledges his first love was boyish
He and Amy reach mutual understanding

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s emotional life shifts from idealized, youthful longing to mature, reciprocal love. The arc is less about replacing one person than about learning what love can realistically be.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From playful charm to ethical responsibility
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Starts as a witty, affectionate boy whose goodness is real but mostly expressed through charm, fun, and spontaneous kindness.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a morally serious adult who thinks in terms of duty, usefulness, charity, and the responsible use of wealth and influence.

trajectory.position_description: He is generous and helpful, but his goodness is mostly social and immediate: flowers, music, parties, and companionship.
key_moments: Offers the carriage and helps the March girls
Hosts the club and pleasure party
Supports Beth's music and the family's cheer

trajectory.position_description: Crisis makes his moral instincts more explicit. He feels responsible for his grandfather, acts decisively in emergencies, and begins to see that his behavior matters beyond amusement.
key_moments: Chooses to stay with Mr. Laurence
Comforts Jo and Amy during Beth's illness

trajectory.position_description: He now thinks in terms of discreet beneficence and practical support for others. Wealth becomes a tool for moral action rather than display.
key_moments: Plans to use money for deserving people
Supports Jo's school and needy boys
Acts as a responsible husband and patron

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s kindness is present from the start, but it becomes more explicitly ethical over time. He moves from charming generosity to a conscious, duty-based moral outlook.

relational_axes.axis_name: From playful fascination to transformed lifelong affection
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as bashful attraction and intense companionship, with Jo as the person who most fully awakens his sense of ease, admiration, and romantic possibility.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as affectionate, non-possessive friendship and mature gratitude, with the romantic charge transformed into stable family-like love.

trajectory.position_description: He is drawn to Jo's frankness, wit, and energy; their bond is playful, intimate, and emotionally central to his life.
key_moments: Special attention to Jo's moods and talents

trajectory.position_description: He remains her closest companion and confidant, but the bond becomes more emotionally loaded as he matures and she becomes more independent.
key_moments: Teases her about marriage and writing
Jo continues to treat him as her best friend

trajectory.position_description: His proposal is refused, producing heartbreak, wounded pride, and a temporary emotional withdrawal.
He no longer seeks Jo romantically; instead, he loves her as family and friend, with warmth, respect, and no jealousy.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s most important relationship arc moves from intimate youthful attraction to painful rejection and finally to a stable, affectionate, non-romantic bond.

relational_axes.axis_name: From teasing acquaintance to chosen life partner
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as friendly amusement and mild affection, with Amy part of the March circle but not his primary emotional focus.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as deep romantic commitment and marital partnership, with Amy as his chosen companion and equal.

trajectory.position_description: He treats Amy as a pleasant, clever, and amusing member of the family circle, with no major romantic emphasis.
Amy becomes more visible as a young woman of substance; he is drawn to her maturity, wit, and social intelligence, especially after his emotional collapse over Jo.
key_moments: Amy's letters and company revive him
He begins to see her as a woman, not a child

trajectory.position_description: Their relationship becomes openly romantic and then settled in marriage, marked by mutual respect, shared values, and domestic contentment.
key_moments: He realizes his love for Jo has faded
He and Amy understand each other clearly

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Amy’s relationship with Laurie evolves from friendly teasing into a mature, reciprocal marriage grounded in shared discipline and affection.

relational_axes.axis_name: From sheltered grandson to dutiful companion
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as a somewhat confined, dependent boy who chafes under his grandfather's authority and feels trapped by his life.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as a grateful, responsible adult who respects his grandfather, accepts duty, and remains emotionally aligned with him.

trajectory.position_description: He is bored, rebellious, and occasionally resentful of the restrictions of home and business life.
He sees his grandfather's loneliness and dependence more clearly and begins to feel morally responsible for him.
key_moments: Decides to stay with Mr. Laurence

trajectory.position_description: He becomes more disciplined and socially mature, living in a way that honors his grandfather's care and expectations.
key_moments: Jo's letters describe him as improved
He remains a respectful, affectionate grandson

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s bond with Mr. Laurence changes from resistance and dependence toward dutiful companionship and mutual respect.

relational_axes.axis_name: From neighboring outsider to quasi-family member
relational_axes.pole_start: Starts as a curious neighbor and occasional visitor who longs for the warmth he sees from outside.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as an integrated family member in all but name, trusted in crises, welcomed in rituals, and included in the household's emotional and practical life.

trajectory.position_description: The Marches are initially a source of fascination and emotional hunger. He watches them, receives their kindness indirectly, and begins to want entry into their world.
Through gifts, rescues, shared games, and crisis support, he becomes a regular and valued presence in the household.
His marriage to Amy completes his transition from guest to kin. He is now part of the family not by proximity alone but by permanent relational membership.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Laurie’s arc with the March family is one of progressive belonging. He moves from longing at the threshold to full participation in their domestic and emotional life.
